clue.text: Signs of the time in the cupboard

indicators.note: in places the period of time inside the word for the cupboard

parts.note: a press is a cupboard, especially one for linen or clothes
an age is a time or era

explanation.surface: A clue about portents of the era found inside a household cupboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Omens or portents that foretell events are what the clue calls signs.

clue.text: Frenchman who painted a topless bridal outfit

indicators.note: topless removes the top, the first letter, in a down clue

parts.note: a trousseau is the clothes and linen a bride assembles

explanation.surface: A French artist depicts a bride's revealing outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' drops the first letter, T, from TROUSSEAU. Henri Rousseau was the French naive painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri, nicknamed Le Douanier, was a French post-impressionist artist.

clue.text: Omitting a line from training aid '

parts.note: skipping means leaving out
a rope is a line

explanation.surface: Leaving a line out of training equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Boxers and athletes jump over a turning cord to build fitness.

clue.text: Beverage supplied by' inexperienced char

parts.note: green means new or inexperienced
char is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A drink made by a novice cleaning lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'char' suggests a charwoman (cleaner); it is slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfermented tea leaves, steeped, make this drink popular in China and Japan.

clue.text: If not a feast, at least a skinful

definitions.text: If not a feast, at least a skinful

parts.words: If not a feast, at least a skinful
parts.note: a skin packed full of minced meat, a modest meal rather than a banquet

explanation.surface: A drinker's remark: no banquet, but plenty to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skinful' usually means a lot of alcohol; here it is a casing filled with meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Minced meat stuffed into a casing makes a skin that is literally full.

clue.text: Injury made Goodfellow fall

parts.note: a good fellow is a saint, abbreviated ST
rain is a fall from the sky

explanation.surface: A tumble by someone named Goodfellow caused harm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goodfellow' reads as a surname (Robin Goodfellow is Puck) but splits as good fellow, a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulled muscle or overstretched ligament is a common sports hurt.

clue.text: American friend 'e met in Cornwall

parts.note: bud, short for buddy, is US slang for a friend
the dropped-aitch form of he, leaving just the vowel

explanation.surface: A Yank's pal says he was met in Cornwall.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside resort town on the north coast of the county lies in Cornwall.

clue.text: Girl Agamemnon captured, shy, cries pitifully

indicators.note: pitifully suggests the words shy and cries are wrecked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A timid captive girl weeps under Agamemnon's control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitifully' rearranges SHY + CRIES. In the Iliad Agamemnon's refusal to return her brought plague on the Greeks.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer she is the priest's daughter seized as a prize by the Greek commander.

clue.text: Notwithstanding, we see Hugh a lot disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed suggests the letters of Hugh and a lot are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone notes that Hugh is greatly upset, despite everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' shuffles HUGH plus ALOT together; 'we see' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are conjunctions meaning in spite of the fact that.

clue.text: An American backs a Muslim

indicators.note: backs means the two pieces are read in reverse order, back to front

parts.note: an is an archaic word for if, as in Shakespeare's 'an it please you'

explanation.surface: An American person supports a follower of Islam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backs' turns IF + US into SUFI. The archaic 'an' meaning 'if' is the trap: it reads as a mere article.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sufi is a Muslim mystic, a follower of the ascetic branch of Islam.

clue.text: Paper gods our law-makers look up to?

parts.note: the press means newspapers collectively
the gods is the top gallery of a theatre

explanation.surface: It suggests MPs revere newspaper deities.
explanation.walkthrough: In the House of Commons the reporters sit in a gallery above the members, so the law-makers literally look up at it; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: The reporters' seating overlooks the Commons chamber, raised above the members.

clue.text: Thrashes the British premier with the French toadies

parts.note: licks means beats or thrashes
William Pitt was a British prime minister
les is French for the, plural

explanation.surface: Sycophants beat a Prime Minister in alliance with France.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsequious flatterers are pictured fawning so low as to lick another's spittle.

clue.text: Protective coating is in support

indicators.note: in places the word is inside the word for support

parts.note: a rest is a support, as for a snooker cue or an arm

explanation.surface: A coating that protects is part of a support.
explanation.definitionFit: In etching and electronics a resist is a substance applied to shield a surface from acid or dye.

clue.text: Gone, twisted side, it's said, killing the race

indicators.note: twisted means the letters of gone are bent into a new order
it's said signals that the following word is only heard, then spelt differently

parts.note: the word side is pronounced like the ending spelt c-i-d-e

explanation.surface: Someone has gone, with a warped side, in a grim account of racial slaughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twisted' turns GONE into GENO; 'it's said' makes SIDE sound like CIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: The deliberate slaughter of a whole people or ethnic group is the term coined for this crime.

clue.text: Old nocturnal swagman

parts.note: swag is loot, so a man carrying swag by night is a house-breaker, not an Australian tramp

explanation.surface: An old Australian vagrant who wanders by night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swagman' suggests an Australian tramp with his bundle; here swag is stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief who breaks into houses, traditionally at night, carries off the swag.

clue.text: Will they grow up to attend on Proctor?

definitions.text: Will they grow up to attend on Proctor?

parts.words: Will they grow up to attend on Proctor?
parts.note: a proctor's attendants at Oxford and Cambridge are called bulldogs, so young ones might grow up into that job

explanation.surface: Asking whether some youngsters will become a university official's assistants.
explanation.walkthrough: A proctor polices students at Oxford or Cambridge, helped by porters nicknamed bulldogs.
explanation.definitionFit: Young bulldogs, the dogs' namesakes being the proctor's university attendants.

clue.text: The Furies gave him no rest and ease, we hear

indicators.note: we hear marks the words as being spoken, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: said quickly, '(n)o rest 'n' ease' approximates the Greek hero's name

explanation.surface: The avenging Furies hounded a man without peace.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Orestes killed his mother Clytemnestra and was pursued by the Furies.
explanation.definitionFit: Greek legend has the avenging spirits pursue Agamemnon's son for matricide.

clue.text: Criminal's radio

definitions.meaning: one who handles stolen goods, a fence
a set that picks up broadcast signals

explanation.definitionFit: A fence takes in stolen property, and a wireless set takes in signals.

clue.text: Pull out Tonga eel — cook well

indicators.note: cook well tells us to stir the words Tonga and eel thoroughly into a new mix

explanation.surface: A recipe: extract an eel from Tonga and cook it properly.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch or lengthen something is to draw it out.

clue.text: Moonshiner's answers ?

parts.note: an illicit distiller uses glass vessels for distilling, and the same word means sharp replies

explanation.surface: Replies given by a bootlegger.
explanation.definitionFit: Distillation flasks and witty comebacks share one plural noun.

clue.text: Drink for a Scotsman of our time, in general

indicators.note: in places the Scotsman and the era inside the general

parts.note: Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general
mon is the Scots form of man
AD, anno Domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: A beverage for a modern Scot, in broad terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in general' looks like 'generally' but means inside a general's name, LEE.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft drink made with lemon juice, sugar and water.

clue.text: Loved trouble — a danger sign

parts.note: ado means fuss or trouble
red is the colour signalling danger

explanation.surface: Romance brought trouble, a warning signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cherished or doted on is the past tense of worship.

clue.text: Church club presents " The Centaur "

parts.note: an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: A church social group stages a play called The Centaur.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Chiron was the wise centaur who tutored Achilles.

clue.text: Head student with claim to divine faculties

definitions.text: Head student with claim to divine faculties

parts.words: Head student with claim to divine faculties
parts.note: one who studies heads, claiming to read mental powers from the bumps of the skull

explanation.surface: A head pupil who claims god-given powers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head student' suggests a head boy or girl; 'divine' is the verb, to discern, not godly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian pseudoscience held that skull contours revealed character and mental capacities.

clue.text: "His rash fierce blaze of — cannot last" (Richard II)

definitions.text: "His rash fierce blaze of — cannot last" (Richard II)

parts.words: "His rash fierce blaze of — cannot last" (Richard II)
parts.note: John of Gaunt's speech on the king's dissipation fills the gap with a word for wild revelry

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare with a word missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrestrained revelry or dissipation is the word Gaunt uses of the young king.

clue.text: King of nonsense

parts.note: both Shakespeare's mad king and Edward, the Victorian writer of nonsense verse and limericks

explanation.surface: A monarch of absurdity.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward of that surname popularised limericks and nonsense verse; the name is also Shakespeare's tragic king.

clue.text: Sinhalese view that pleased Bishop Heber

definitions.text: Sinhalese view that pleased Bishop Heber

parts.words: Sinhalese view that pleased Bishop Heber
parts.note: Heber's hymn 'From Greenland's Icy Mountains' says of Ceylon that every view pleases and only man is vile

explanation.surface: A Ceylonese scene that delighted a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: Sinhalese means of Ceylon (Sri Lanka); the hymn line is 'Though every prospect pleases, and only man is vile'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hymn's word for the scenery of Ceylon is a synonym for a vista.

clue.text: Forces the opening of safety locks

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: tresses are locks of hair

explanation.surface: Strong measures are needed to open secure locks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' looks like a verb or security device; it means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressures or strains acting on a structure are the engineering sense of the plural noun.
